1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""validate-task-schema.py
3	
4	Validate that geeky-plan task files (tasks/Tx-*.md) carry the sections the
5	template defines and that geeky-implement relies on. This is the plan->implement
6	boundary gate: run it at the end of geeky-plan and the start of geeky-implement.
7	
8	Required sections (missing => ERROR, file fails):
9	  Task Name, Scope / In scope, Dependencies, Acceptance Criteria,
10	  Tests/Validation Before Next Task, Priority
11	Recommended sections (missing => WARNING):
12	  Context, Module/System, Technical Notes, Definition of Done, Estimate
13	
14	Matching is tolerant: a label counts as present if any line, after stripping
15	leading '#'/'*' markers and whitespace, begins with the label (case-insensitive).
16	
17	Contract (matches the other validators):
18	  argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
19	  --json emits a machine-readable object.
20	
21	Usage:
22	  python validate-task-schema.py --path "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder"
23	  python validate-task-schema.py --file "/abs/path/to/tasks/T1-foo.md" --json
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import argparse
29	import json
30	import re
31	import sys
32	from pathlib import Path
33	
34	REQUIRED = (
35	    ("Task Name", r"Task\s*Name"),
36	    ("In scope", r"In\s*scope"),
37	    ("Dependencies", r"Dependencies"),
38	    ("Acceptance Criteria", r"Acceptance\s*Criteria"),
39	    ("Tests/Validation", r"Tests\s*/\s*Validation"),
40	    ("Priority", r"Priority"),
41	)
42	RECOMMENDED = (
43	    ("Context", r"Context"),
44	    ("Module/System", r"Module\s*/\s*System"),
45	    ("Technical Notes", r"Technical\s*Notes"),
46	    ("Definition of Done", r"Definition\s+of\s+Done"),
47	    ("Estimate", r"Estimate"),
48	)
49	
50	NOTES_RE = re.compile(r"\.notes\.md$", re.IGNORECASE)
51	
52	
53	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
54	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
55	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path", required=False)
56	    p.add_argument("positional", nargs="?", default=None)
57	    p.add_argument("--file", dest="file", required=False)
58	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
59	    return p.parse_args()
60	
61	
62	def label_present(text: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
63	    rx = re.compile(rf"^\s*[#*\s]*{pattern}\b", re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)
64	    return rx.search(text) is not None
65	
66	
67	def check_file(path: Path) -> dict:
68	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
69	    missing_required = [name for name, pat in REQUIRED if not label_present(text, pat)]
70	    missing_recommended = [name for name, pat in RECOMMENDED if not label_present(text, pat)]
71	    return {
72	        "file": path.name,
73	        "ok": not missing_required,
74	        "missing_required": missing_required,
75	        "missing_recommended": missing_recommended,
76	    }
77	
78	
79	def collect_task_files(folder: Path) -> list[Path]:
80	    tasks_dir = folder / "tasks"
81	    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
82	        return []
83	    return sorted(
84	        f for f in tasks_dir.iterdir()
85	        if f.is_file() and f.name.lower().endswith(".md") and not NOTES_RE.search(f.name)
86	        and f.name[:1].upper() == "T"
87	    )
88	
89	
90	def main() -> int:
91	    args = parse_args()
92	
93	    files: list[Path] = []
94	    if args.file:
95	        files = [Path(args.file)]
96	    else:
97	        path_str = args.path or args.positional
98	        if not path_str:
99	            print("USAGE: validate-task-schema.py (--path <folder> | --file <task.md>) [--json]")
100	            return 1
101	        folder = Path(path_str)
102	        if not folder.is_dir():
103	            msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
104	            print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
105	            return 1
106	        files = collect_task_files(folder)
107	
108	    if not files:
109	        msg = "NO_TASK_FILES: nothing to validate (expected tasks/Tx-*.md)"
110	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
111	        return 1
112	
113	    results = []
114	    for f in files:
115	        if not f.is_file():
116	            results.append({"file": str(f), "ok": False,
117	                            "missing_required": ["<file not found>"], "missing_recommended": []})
118	            continue
119	        results.append(check_file(f))
120	
121	    ok = all(r["ok"] for r in results)
122	    failed = sum(1 for r in results if not r["ok"])
123	
124	    if args.as_json:
125	        print(json.dumps({"ok": ok, "results": results}, indent=2))
126	    else:
127	        prefix = "OK" if ok else "INVALID_TASK_SCHEMA"
128	        print(f"{prefix}: {len(results)} task file(s) checked, {failed} failing.")
129	        for r in results:
130	            if r["missing_required"]:
131	                print(f"  {r['file']}:")
132	                for m in r["missing_required"]:
133	                    print(f"    ERROR:   missing required section: {m}")
134	            for m in r["missing_recommended"]:
135	                print(f"    WARNING: {r['file']} missing recommended section: {m}")
136	
137	    return 0 if ok else 1
138	
139	
140	if __name__ == "__main__":
141	    sys.exit(main())
142

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""validate-kanban.py
3	
4	Deterministic integrity check for a geeky-plan kanban.md against the tasks/ folder.
5	Replaces LLM self-report ("I updated the board") with a fail-stop check.
6	
7	Checks (errors fail the run; warnings do not):
8	  ERROR   - a task file in tasks/ is not placed in any lane (untracked)
9	  ERROR   - a task id appears in more than one lane (ambiguous placement)
10	  WARNING - a task id referenced in the kanban has no matching task file (dangling)
11	  WARNING - In Progress count exceeds the WIP cap (default 3)
12	  WARNING - a known lane heading is entirely missing
13	
14	Recognised lanes (case-insensitive, any heading depth): Backlog, Ready,
15	In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done. A heading containing "validation" is
16	treated as the release-gate checklist, not a task lane.
17	
18	Contract (matches the other validators):
19	  argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
20	  --json emits a machine-readable object instead of the human summary.
21	
22	Usage:
23	  python validate-kanban.py --path "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder"
24	  python validate-kanban.py "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder" --wip 3 --json
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	import argparse
30	import json
31	import re
32	import sys
33	from pathlib import Path
34	
35	# Ordered so that more specific "In ..." lanes are tested before short names.
36	KNOWN_LANES = ("Backlog", "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review", "Blocked", "Done")
37	
38	HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
39	TASK_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\bT\d+\b", re.IGNORECASE)
40	TASK_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"^T\d+", re.IGNORECASE)
41	NOTES_RE = re.compile(r"\.notes\.md$", re.IGNORECASE)
42	
43	
44	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
45	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
46	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path", required=False)
47	    p.add_argument("positional", nargs="?", default=None)
48	    p.add_argument("--wip", type=int, default=3, help="In Progress WIP cap (default 3)")
49	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
50	    return p.parse_args()
51	
52	
53	def lane_for_heading(heading: str) -> str | None:
54	    """Return the canonical lane name for a heading, or None."""
55	    norm = heading.strip().lower()
56	    if "validation" in norm:
57	        return None
58	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
59	        if norm == lane.lower() or norm.startswith(lane.lower()):
60	            return lane
61	    return None
62	
63	
64	def task_ids_from_files(tasks_dir: Path) -> set[str]:
65	    ids: set[str] = set()
66	    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
67	        return ids
68	    for f in tasks_dir.iterdir():
69	        if not f.is_file():
70	            continue
71	        if NOTES_RE.search(f.name) or not f.name.lower().endswith(".md"):
72	            continue
73	        m = TASK_FILE_RE.match(f.name)
74	        if m:
75	            ids.add(m.group(0).upper())
76	    return ids
77	
78	
79	def parse_kanban(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, set[str]], set[str]]:
80	    """Map canonical lane -> set of task ids referenced under it, and the set of
81	    lane headings actually present in the document."""
82	    placements: dict[str, set[str]] = {lane: set() for lane in KNOWN_LANES}
83	    present: set[str] = set()
84	    current: str | None = None
85	    for line in text.splitlines():
86	        hm = HEADING_RE.match(line)
87	        if hm:
88	            current = lane_for_heading(hm.group(1))
89	            if current:
90	                present.add(current)
91	            continue
92	        if current is None:
93	            continue
94	        for tid in TASK_ID_RE.findall(line):
95	            placements[current].add(tid.upper())
96	    return placements, present
97	
98	
99	def build_report(folder: Path, wip_cap: int) -> dict:
100	    errors: list[str] = []
101	    warnings: list[str] = []
102	
103	    kanban = folder / "kanban.md"
104	    if not kanban.is_file():
105	        return {
106	            "ok": False,
107	            "errors": [f"MISSING: {kanban}"],
108	            "warnings": [],
109	            "lane_counts": {},
110	            "summary": f"INVALID_KANBAN: {kanban} not found.",
111	        }
112	
113	    file_ids = task_ids_from_files(folder / "tasks")
114	    placements, present_lanes = parse_kanban(
115	        kanban.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
116	    )
117	
118	    # Where does each id live?
119	    id_lanes: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
120	    for lane, ids in placements.items():
121	        for tid in ids:
122	            id_lanes.setdefault(tid, []).append(lane)
123	
124	    # Untracked: a real task file not placed anywhere.
125	    for tid in sorted(file_ids):
126	        if tid not in id_lanes:
127	            errors.append(f"{tid} has a task file but is not placed in any kanban lane")
128	
129	    # Ambiguous: placed in more than one lane.
130	    for tid, lanes in sorted(id_lanes.items()):
131	        if len(lanes) > 1:
132	            errors.append(f"{tid} appears in multiple lanes: {', '.join(sorted(lanes))}")
133	
134	    # Dangling: referenced in kanban but no task file.
135	    for tid in sorted(id_lanes):
136	        if file_ids and tid not in file_ids:
137	            warnings.append(f"{tid} is referenced in the kanban but has no tasks/{tid}-*.md file")
138	
139	    # Missing lanes.
140	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
141	        if lane not in present_lanes:
142	            warnings.append(f'lane "{lane}" heading not found in kanban.md')
143	
144	    # WIP cap.
145	    in_progress = len(placements["In Progress"])
146	    if in_progress > wip_cap:
147	        warnings.append(f"In Progress has {in_progress} tasks (WIP cap {wip_cap})")
148	
149	    lane_counts = {lane: len(ids) for lane, ids in placements.items()}
150	    tracked = len({tid for ids in placements.values() for tid in ids})
151	
152	    ok = not errors
153	    summary = (
154	        f"{'OK' if ok else 'INVALID_KANBAN'}: {tracked} task(s) tracked, "
155	        f"{len(file_ids)} task file(s). "
156	        + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in lane_counts.items())
157	    )
158	    return {
159	        "ok": ok,
160	        "errors": errors,
161	        "warnings": warnings,
162	        "lane_counts": lane_counts,
163	        "summary": summary,
164	    }
165	
166	
167	def main() -> int:
168	    args = parse_args()
169	    path_str = args.path or args.positional
170	    if not path_str:
171	        print("USAGE: validate-kanban.py --path <folder> [--wip N] [--json]")
172	        return 1
173	
174	    folder = Path(path_str)
175	    if not folder.is_dir():
176	        msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
177	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
178	        return 1
179	
180	    report = build_report(folder, args.wip)
181	
182	    if args.as_json:
183	        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
184	    else:
185	        print(report["summary"])
186	        for e in report["errors"]:
187	            print(f"  ERROR:   {e}")
188	        for w in report["warnings"]:
189	            print(f"  WARNING: {w}")
190	
191	    return 0 if report["ok"] else 1
192	
193	
194	if __name__ == "__main__":
195	    sys.exit(main())
196

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""validate-planning-folder.py
3	
4	Verify that a folder produced by /geeky-plan contains all artifacts /geeky-implement needs.
5	
6	Exit codes (match validate-planning-folder.ps1 exactly):
7	  0  -> OK summary on stdout, folder is valid
8	  1  -> missing-artifact summary on stdout, folder is invalid
9	
10	Usage:
11	  python validate-planning-folder.py --path "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder"
12	  python validate-planning-folder.py "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder"   # positional also supported
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import argparse
18	import json
19	import os
20	import re
21	import sys
22	from pathlib import Path
23	
24	
25	REQUIRED = (
26	    "implementation-plan.md",
27	    "kanban.md",
28	    "references.md",
29	    "handoff.md",
30	)
31	
32	RECOMMENDED = (
33	    "feature-specification.md",
34	    "draft.md",
35	)
36	
37	# Match the .ps1: tasks/T*-*.md but exclude the *.notes.md siblings.
38	TASK_INCLUDE = re.compile(r"^T.*\.md$", re.IGNORECASE)
39	TASK_EXCLUDE = re.compile(r"\.notes\.md$", re.IGNORECASE)
40	
41	
42	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
43	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
44	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path", required=False)
45	    p.add_argument("positional", nargs="?", default=None)
46	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
47	    return p.parse_args()
48	
49	
50	def main() -> int:
51	    args = parse_args()
52	    path_str = args.path or args.positional
53	    if not path_str:
54	        msg = "USAGE: validate-planning-folder.py --path <folder> [--json]"
55	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
56	        return 1
57	
58	    folder = Path(path_str)
59	    if not folder.is_dir():
60	        msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
61	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
62	        return 1
63	
64	    missing: list[str] = []
65	    for name in REQUIRED:
66	        if not (folder / name).is_file():
67	            missing.append(name)
68	
69	    tasks_dir = folder / "tasks"
70	    task_count = 0
71	    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
72	        missing.append("tasks/ (directory)")
73	    else:
74	        task_files = [
75	            f for f in tasks_dir.iterdir()
76	            if f.is_file() and TASK_INCLUDE.match(f.name) and not TASK_EXCLUDE.search(f.name)
77	        ]
78	        task_count = len(task_files)
79	        if task_count == 0:
80	            missing.append("tasks/Tx-*.md (no task files found)")
81	
82	    missing_recommended = [
83	        name for name in RECOMMENDED if not (folder / name).is_file()
84	    ]
85	
86	    ok = not missing
87	    if args.as_json:

2	"""check-dod.py
3	
4	Definition-of-Done checker for a single geeky-implement task. Embodies "verify,
5	don't trust": instead of believing the agent that a task is finished, assert the
6	durable signals on disk before the task may move to Done.
7	
8	Checks for task <ID> in <folder> (missing => ERROR unless noted):
9	  - a per-task notes file tasks/<ID>-*.notes.md exists
10	  - <ID> is placed in the Done lane of kanban.md
11	  - handoff.md mentions <ID>
12	  - WARNING if <ID> still appears in a non-Done lane (In Progress / Blocked / ...)
13	
14	It also extracts and prints the task's "Tests/Validation Before Next Task" block
15	so the orchestrator can re-run those commands itself (this script does not execute
16	them — running is the caller's job, kept framework- and shell-agnostic).
17	
18	Contract: argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
19	  --json emits a machine-readable object.
20	
21	Usage:
22	  python check-dod.py --path "/abs/docs/feature" --task T3
23	  python check-dod.py "/abs/docs/feature" T3 --json
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import argparse
29	import json
30	import re
31	import sys
32	from pathlib import Path
33	
34	KNOWN_LANES = ("Backlog", "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review", "Blocked", "Done")
35	HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
36	
37	
38	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
39	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
40	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path")
41	    p.add_argument("--task", dest="task")
42	    p.add_argument("pos_path", nargs="?", default=None)
43	    p.add_argument("pos_task", nargs="?", default=None)
44	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
45	    return p.parse_args()
46	
47	
48	def lane_for_heading(heading: str) -> str | None:
49	    norm = heading.strip().lower()
50	    if "validation" in norm:
51	        return None
52	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
53	        if norm == lane.lower() or norm.startswith(lane.lower()):
54	            return lane
55	    return None
56	
57	
58	def lanes_for_task(kanban_text: str, task_id: str) -> list[str]:
59	    found: list[str] = []
60	    current: str | None = None
61	    tid_re = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(task_id)}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
62	    for line in kanban_text.splitlines():
63	        hm = HEADING_RE.match(line)
64	        if hm:
65	            current = lane_for_heading(hm.group(1))
66	            continue
67	        if current and tid_re.search(line) and current not in found:
68	            found.append(current)
69	    return found
70	
71	
72	def extract_validation_block(task_text: str) -> str:
73	    lines = task_text.splitlines()
74	    start = None
75	    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
76	        if re.search(r"Tests\s*/\s*Validation", line, re.IGNORECASE):
77	            start = i + 1
78	            break
79	    if start is None:
80	        return ""
81	    out: list[str] = []
82	    for line in lines[start:]:
83	        # Stop at the next section label (Estimate:/Priority:/heading).
84	        if re.match(r"^\s*[#*\s]*(Estimate|Priority)\b", line, re.IGNORECASE):
85	            break
86	        if re.match(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+\S", line):
87	            break
88	        out.append(line)
89	    return "\n".join(out).strip()
90	
91	
92	def main() -> int:
93	    args = parse_args()
94	    path_str = args.path or args.pos_path
95	    task_id = (args.task or args.pos_task or "").upper()
96	    if not path_str or not task_id:
97	        print("USAGE: check-dod.py --path <folder> --task <ID> [--json]")
98	        return 1
99	
100	    folder = Path(path_str)
101	    if not folder.is_dir():
102	        msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
103	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
104	        return 1
105	
106	    errors: list[str] = []
107	    warnings: list[str] = []
108	
109	    # 1. notes file
110	    tasks_dir = folder / "tasks"
111	    notes = []
112	    if tasks_dir.is_dir():
113	        notes = [f.name for f in tasks_dir.iterdir()
114	                 if f.is_file() and re.match(rf"^{re.escape(task_id)}\b", f.name, re.IGNORECASE)
115	                 and f.name.lower().endswith(".notes.md")]
116	    if not notes:
117	        errors.append(f"no per-task notes file tasks/{task_id}-*.notes.md")
118	
119	    # 2/4. kanban placement
120	    kanban = folder / "kanban.md"
121	    lanes: list[str] = []
122	    if not kanban.is_file():
123	        errors.append("kanban.md not found")
124	    else:
125	        lanes = lanes_for_task(kanban.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), task_id)
126	        if "Done" not in lanes:
127	            errors.append(f"{task_id} is not in the Done lane (found in: {', '.join(lanes) or 'no lane'})")
128	        non_done = [l for l in lanes if l != "Done"]
129	        if non_done:
130	            warnings.append(f"{task_id} also appears in: {', '.join(non_done)}")
131	
132	    # 3. handoff mention
133	    handoff = folder / "handoff.md"
134	    if not handoff.is_file():
135	        warnings.append("handoff.md not found")
136	    elif not re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(task_id)}\b", handoff.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), re.IGNORECASE):
137	        warnings.append(f"handoff.md does not mention {task_id}")
138	
139	    # validation block (informational)
140	    validation = ""
141	    if tasks_dir.is_dir():
142	        for f in tasks_dir.iterdir():
143	            if (f.is_file() and re.match(rf"^{re.escape(task_id)}\b", f.name, re.IGNORECASE)
144	                    and f.name.lower().endswith(".md") and not f.name.lower().endswith(".notes.md")):
145	                validation = extract_validation_block(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
146	                break
147	
148	    ok = not errors
149	    summary = f"{'DOD_OK' if ok else 'DOD_INCOMPLETE'}: {task_id}"
150	
151	    if args.as_json:
152	        print(json.dumps({
153	            "ok": ok, "task": task_id, "errors": errors, "warnings": warnings,
154	            "lanes": lanes, "validation_block": validation,
155	        }, indent=2))
156	    else:
157	        print(summary)
158	        for e in errors:
159	            print(f"  ERROR:   {e}")
160	        for w in warnings:
161	            print(f"  WARNING: {w}")
162	        if validation:
163	            print("  Re-run this task's validation block (verify, don't trust):")
164	            for line in validation.splitlines():
165	                print(f"    | {line}")
166

# minisql Implementation Plan

## Authority and outcome

Implement the entire root `contract.md` R1–R21 / AC1–AC12, with the architecture and pytest requirement in `brief.md`. The feature specification organizes but cannot override that authority. No required scope is deferred. Decisions D1–D7 in feature-specification.md §8 resolve unspecified edges; an explicit contract rule always wins.

## Architecture and ownership

| Surface | Owner | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| minisql/errors.py, model.py, lexer.py, ast.py, parser.py, initial __init__.py | T1 | Error classes, frozen Result, positioned tokens, source-preserving AST/parser |
| minisql/catalog.py | T2 | Directory discovery, strict CSV loading and inference |
| minisql/formatting.py | T3 | Pure exact CSV and aligned-table strings |
| minisql/semantic.py, executor.py, connection.py; final __init__.py | T4 | Typed/bound analysis, ordered execution, public API integration |
| minisql/__main__.py, cli.py, root README.md | T5 | One-shot/REPL and usage documentation |
| tests/test_contract.py, test_regressions.py, test_imports.py | T6 | Independent contract-wide acceptance/regression coverage |

Each task owns its corresponding test files as listed in the task. Workers may not edit another task's surface without orchestrator coordination and recording the consequence in both task notes and handoff. Orchestrator does not edit product code/tests; fixes return to geeky-coder.

## Cross-module integration contract

### Foundation protocol

T1 exposes `MiniSQLError(message, line=None, column=None)` and subclasses with class-specific kinds; subclasses accept message then line/column. `DataIOError(message)` has None positions. Attributes and str formatting exactly contract. `model.Result` is frozen dataclass with list columns, list types, list tuple rows. Initial __init__ exports Result and errors only, avoiding imports of modules not yet present.

T1 chooses and documents concrete lexer/AST/parser interfaces in T1 notes. They must expose token kind/raw text/decoded value/start/end/line/column, parser entry `parse(sql) -> Query` (lexer may be invoked inside), complete AST for contract grammar, distinct parenthesis metadata, source spans and operator/name/star/ESCAPE tokens. Preserve raw source for output heading and resolved-independent structure. T4 consumes those interfaces; T1 notes are a required handoff, not a change to the frozen task body.

### Data protocol

T2 exposes `Catalog(data_dir)` (immediate validation), `tables() -> list[str]`, `load(name, line=1, column=1) -> Table`, `schema(name)` where Table has name, columns list[str], types list[str], rows list[tuple]. Unknown table raises SemanticError at provided coordinates; ambiguous/corrupt data DataIOError. A load call rereads disk; executor may reuse a table within one execute but never across execute calls. Semantic analysis loads table refs in FROM order and resolves range names itself.

T2 imports errors from errors.py; no dependency on parser/semantic. During the independent phase tests may use the agreed protocol when T1 is simultaneously creating errors; collect integration validation after all workers return.

### Formatting protocol

T3 implements `format_csv(result: Result) -> str` and `format_table(result: Result) -> str` in formatting.py, imports Result from model only, never touches streams. T3 tests may construct Result. It must exactly preserve NULL/empty TEXT distinction.

### Engine protocol

T4 exposes `Connection(data_dir)`, connect, execute, tables/schema and full __init__ API. Execute obtains AST, binds all references/types before executor calls. Semantic and executor must remain distinct recognizable layers; implementation may use bound node records or annotations but must preserve raw AST source metadata. Formats reexported from formatting. No import-time stream mutation.

## Implementation phases and dependency graph

### Phase 1 — Foundations (T1, T2, T3)

Dispatch up to three independent non-overlapping workers concurrently. T2 and T3 share only agreed protocols; T1 creates errors/model promptly. No worker edits shared __init__ except T1. Completion commands cover all three surfaces after return. All stay In Review until a single reviewer subagent gives individual task verdicts and phase `READY TO ADVANCE`. Then Done + check-dod/kanban gates and phase commit.

### Phase 2 — Typed engine (T4)

Depends on Done T1/T2/T3 and phase-1 READY. Implement binder and explicit executor pipeline together because resolved identities, aggregate slots and execution contexts are tightly coupled. Largest task; split internally into analysis then execution, but its scope is fully specified. Use exact contract, not a generic SQL engine. Independent reviewer checks all T4 ACs and collective engine requirements, returns task verdict plus READY TO ADVANCE. Fixes by coder only. Then Done/gates and phase commit.

### Phase 3 — Delivery and acceptance (T5, T6)

Both depend on Done T4; run concurrently with distinct test/product surfaces. T6 tests engine and format/public API, not T5 CLI until integration; T5 owns subprocess CLI/REPL tests. Collect all, run combined full suite/import/compile checks. Independent reviewer returns both task verdicts and phase READY TO ADVANCE, including contract-wide gaps. Done/gates and phase commit. Final stage remains the separately required three-lane impl-review.

Dependency edges: T1/T2/T3 → T4 → T5/T6. No cycles. T2/T3 use fixed foundational protocols without completion dependency, enabled by common integration validation and no overlapping writes. Worker scheduling must honor explicit task dependencies; Backlog tasks promoted only after dependencies Done.

## Engine design details

### Lex / parse

Handwritten complete lexer, recursive-descent parser. Positions code points, LF-only lines. Exact ASCII regexes, malformed continuation checks; signs separate. Precedence and non-associative comparison exact. Quoted names/strings decode doubles while retaining original spans. Full tokenize before parse. Parenthesis node/flag preserved for headings/bare ORDER but ignored for structural keys. No FROM yields one empty row.

### Semantic

Load referenced CSVs in FROM order after parse; no unrelated reads. Scoped ON binding per introduced prefix; aliases hide original qualifiers, duplicate ranges positioned at second range token. Expand wildcards; preserve output headers. Bind resolved column indexes and static types for every expression irrespective of rows, filters, short circuit or pagination. Type operators and conditions exactly, no bool outputs.

Discover aggregates in select/HAVING/order; reject forbidden placement/nesting/star. Recursively validate grouping by bound structural keys. Group keys compare column identity, operators, typed literal values, operand order; no text matching/algebraic rewriting. Resolve bare ORDER alias/ordinal before input expression binding; alias wins, duplicate aliases ambiguous. DISTINCT restricts order to selected structure or alias/ordinal. Record projected output indexes for alias/ordinal reuse.

### Execute

Materialized stage barriers: joins → WHERE → grouping keys/all aggregate arguments → HAVING → select → ORDER keys → first DISTINCT → stable sort → OFFSET/LIMIT. Nested-loop join order and first-seen group order. Global aggregate group exists even empty. Distinct and grouping equate None; normal predicates do not. All aggregate arguments evaluated in input order before HAVING. All projection before order-key evaluation. LIMIT 0 cannot suppress faults.

Use explicit 3VL; only AND/OR guaranteed short circuit. NULL arithmetic before zero checks; integer quotient exact truncation (abs quotient/sign), remainder dividend-signed; real math.fmod. LIKE whole-string newline-capable matcher with strict ESCAPE policy. Stable multi-key comparator handles NULL and DESC without reversing tie order. Return complete Result before any CLI writes.

### Output / CLI

Custom CSV quoting iff prescribed conditions, not csv.writer defaults. Table escapes before measuring, numeric actual values right, NULL left. CLI reconfigure UTF-8/LF only inside main; argparse usage exit 2. Validate data before SQL lexing. One-shot error stdout empty; engine error one stderr line, codes 1/3. REPL prompt/buffer state follows literal textual suffix and EOF rules, .tables/.schema/.format/help/quit/exit, errors continue.

## Validation strategy

Each task supplies exact pytest commands plus compile checks. `python3` denotes available host interpreter, not a claim that its version satisfies stack target. Record runtime with each suite. Current host default 3.9.6; installed 3.14 variants killed before version output. Product targets >=3.11; maintain compatible stdlib syntax where feasible to enable local checks; do not impose a needless runtime rejection. Seek existing supported interpreter without installation; if unavailable, report as unexecuted-runtime warning and review source compatibility. Windows/Linux byte behavior designed/tested structurally but no unrun OS claimed.

Required task suites: lexer/parser, catalog, formatting, semantic, executor, API, CLI, REPL, contract anchors/regressions/import audit. Final `python3 -m pytest -q`, `python3 -m compileall -q minisql`, and stdlib/no sqlite/SQL-engine audit. Exact numeric outcomes and tested revision/content recorded in notes. Tests for all contract sections, not just examples. No external SQL differential oracle.

## Review / Done / commit gates

Before implementation: validate planning folder, task schema and kanban plus independent plan-review. During work: validate kanban after each lane move. At phase end single independent code-reviewer receives task contracts, worker evidence, concrete changed files and validation commands; returns per-task verdicts and phase READY TO ADVANCE (last phase included). Required fixes coder-owned and reviewed again. Bare claims insufficient; reuse valid revision evidence and rerun invalidated/missing checks.

Move approved task to Done provisionally, check-dod and kanban same step; revert from Done on failure. Notes/handoff mandatory. Commit per phase, message lists task IDs and passes check-commit; attribution per session. Never push/force/amend/no-verify. Preserve frozen artifacts throughout implementation. If Blocked, checkpoint notes/kanban/handoff then stop. Final impl-review separately mandatory, fixes preapproved, repeat until overall PASS or budget/capability blocker.

## Budget and checkpoint policy

Hard deadline 2026-11-04T16:44:18.482771Z; reserve 900s. Research cumulative advisory target 15%, planning 30%, plan-review 40% of usable budget. Planning target 2026-11-04T12:27:48.482771Z. Each stage reads workflow-budget helper at entry/transitions, numbered phases and before/after delegation/waits. Inspect status/action; reserve starts no stage/delegation; invalid/exhausted checkpoint and stop. Targets never acceptance or deadline extension. Pass current exact target/deadline/reserve to all workers/reviewers. Host blocking Agent supports result collection but no wait timeout; record limitation. Checkpoint exact incomplete state, never skip gates to claim done.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/skills/plan-review

Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).

# Plan Review

Multi-phase planning package quality review that validates document alignment, resolves inconsistencies, validates execution sequencing, and performs a final sanity pass. Targets the `/geeky-plan` output folder (implementation-plan.md, kanban.md, tasks/, references.md, review-development-project-manager.md, handoff.md, plus execution-schedule.md if the plan produced one).

## Arguments

Accept a planning folder path (e.g., `docs/feature-name/`). If no argument is given, scan `docs/` for the most recent folder containing an `implementation-plan.md`.

## Time budget and checkpoint

At entry, before each numbered task or phase, after a lengthy direct operation,
and immediately before and after each worker dispatch or blocking wait, run
`python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/workflow-budget.py" --stage plan-review --json`.
Resolve `/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration` to the installed plugin root containing this skill
when the environment variable is unset, and use an available Python interpreter.
If the helper cannot run or its output is unreadable, stop and report the missing
budget check; do not assume unlimited time. Read the JSON status, not just the
exit code: `unbounded` means no deadline was provided; `active` continues; `reserve` or `exhausted` stops starting new work
and checkpoints the incomplete stage; `invalid` stops and reports the configuration
error. A zero exit also covers `reserve`, so it is not permission to continue.
The stage target is advisory, not a gate or guarantee: after it is exceeded,
finish required work with the smallest sufficient evidence and defer optional
expansion. Never skip a required review, validator or acceptance condition, or
claim an incomplete stage passed. Pass the hard deadline, closeout reserve, and
stage target from the check to every child brief. If the deadline is absent, say
unbounded; if only the target is absent, say the target is unavailable. Do not
invent either value. Tell each child to return its current evidence,
unresolved questions and status before the available work time ends. Bound waits by
the remaining usable time where the host supports it; if it cannot, record that
limitation rather than claiming cancellation. Recheck after a wait; a child report alone does not override the budget result.

If the budget stops this stage, preserve the completed review sections and unresolved checks in `review-plan.md` and handoff; do not declare READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION. Resume with the existing invalidation rules.

## Workflow

Execute the four phases in order, except for the safe Phase 2/3 overlap described under Execution Strategy. Each phase uses the findings it depends on.

**Resume contract:** append each phase's output to its existing `review-plan.md` section as it completes (tagged `<!-- phase-N-complete -->`), including reviewer agent ID where applicable, reviewed revision/file hashes, findings and verdict. Reuse completed phases only when their inputs remain valid against a complete diff, including untracked additions; a marker alone is insufficient. Recheck changed content and affected references for local mechanical fixes. Requirement/AC/task-scope/coverage changes invalidate alignment; dependency/order/phase/gate/resource/validation-feasibility changes invalidate sequencing. More than five changed files or cross-document task-ID/dependency/order changes require the full Phase 1 recheck and fresh affected sequencing verdict. Missing baseline/diff, omitted untracked additions, conflicts or unbounded impact require full sanity and fresh affected reviewer verdicts. Record what was reused, rechecked and why; do not re-apply already verified fixes.

---

### Phase 1: Document Alignment Audit

**Pre-flight:** Check for required validator scripts under `/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/` (validate-task-schema.py, validate-kanban.py, validate-planning-folder.py). If `/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration` is unset or scripts are missing, skip to the fallback semantic review below — no blocker.

If scripts are available, run the bundled deterministic validators and treat any non-zero exit as a Critical finding (`python` form works cross-platform; paired `.ps1` scripts exist — see AGENTS.md):

- `python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-task-schema.py" --path "<folder>"`
- `python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"`
- `python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261104T104418Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"`

**Fallback (when scripts unavailable):** Proceed directly to the semantic review below — the subagent performs manual structural checks that scripts would have automated.

Deploy a review subagent for the semantic cross-validation the scripts cannot cover; request concise, actionable findings and evidence rather than restating the package — read the ENTIRE spec/plan folder and cross-validate:

**Files to read:**
- `feature-specification.md` (preferred requirements doc)
- `draft.md` (if present and used by this package)
- `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` (legacy requirements document, if present)
- `implementation-plan.md` — task list, phases/ordering, dependencies
- `kanban.md` — task states and blocked-by relationships
- `execution-schedule.md` (if present)
- `tasks/T*.md` — every task file (title, dependencies, scope, validation block)
- `handoff.md` — status, deviations, next steps
- `references.md` — links (if present)
- `review-development-project-manager.md` — PM review (if present)
- `README.md` — summary (if present)

**Cross-validation checks:**
1. Every task in `implementation-plan.md` has a matching file in `tasks/`
2. Task IDs in `kanban.md` match those in `implementation-plan.md` exactly
3. If the plan defines waves/phases or gate criteria, they are consistent across all documents (their absence is not a finding — the geeky-plan template does not require them)
4. Dependency declarations (`Dependencies:` in task files) are consistent with the plan's ordering; if `Blocks`/wave fields exist, verify they are bidirectionally consistent
5. If `execution-schedule.md` exists, gate criteria match the Tests/Validation blocks in task files
6. Files referenced in tasks actually exist in the codebase (or are explicitly to-be-created)
7. Acceptance criteria in the requirements document are covered by at least one task
8. No orphaned tasks (in task files but not in kanban or plan)
9. No phantom tasks (in kanban/plan but missing task file)
10. **Accuracy** — technical claims match reality (file paths, package names, resource types)
11. **References** — cross-document references point to correct paths, sections and task IDs
12. **Non-conflicting instructions** — documents do not contradict each other on the same topic
13. **Completeness** — table-of-contents sections exist and every “see X” link resolves
14. **Freshness** — dates, versions and task counts are current
15. **Convention adherence** — applicable CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md conventions are reflected in tasks

**Handling optional sections:** If a document contains a section stub marked as optional or placeholder (e.g., "[Optional: X]", "TBD"), do NOT flag it as missing content — optional stubs are valid and expected in planning packages.

**Output:** In `review-plan.md` Phase 1, save the alignment reviewer ID, input revision/file hashes, findings and verdict with severity levels (Critical / Warning / Suggestion, within the plan-review scope).

### Phase 2: Issue Resolution

For each finding from Phase 1:

- **Critical issues** (broken references, missing tasks, contradictory dependencies): Fix immediately by editing the affected document(s).
- **Warnings** (inconsistent wording, unclear gate criteria, missing details): Fix if the correction is unambiguous (see criteria below); flag for user if judgment is required.
- **Suggestions** (style, optional improvements): Note but do not block.

**Unambiguous auto-fix criteria:** A fix is unambiguous when it (a) corrects a mechanical inconsistency (typo, broken link, mismatched ID), (b) does not change task scope or ordering, and (c) has exactly one valid correction. Examples: fixing a task ID typo, adding a missing task file for a declared task, correcting a file path. Requires judgment: rephrasing goals, splitting/merging tasks, reordering dependencies.

After fixes, re-run the deterministic validators (if available), then apply the resume invalidation rules above. A local mechanical correction with bounded impact needs a changed-content/reference check; scope, requirements and sequencing edits need fresh affected verdicts. Preserve independent alignment and sequencing reviewers, including on resume.

**Output:** A table of finding → action taken → status (fixed / flagged / deferred).

### Phase 3: Sequencing & Parallelization Validation

Deploy a **time-master planner** subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-architect` type; fall back to `general-purpose` only if that agent type is unavailable) with this brief:

> Analyze the implementation plan and task files for sequencing correctness. The package declares ordering via task numbering (`Tx-`) and `Dependencies:` fields; derive the execution structure from those. Validate:
>
> 1. **Dependency graph is acyclic** — no circular dependencies
> 2. **Critical path** — derive the longest dependency chain; if the plan states one, verify it matches
> 3. **Parallelization opportunities are maximized** — derive groups of mutually independent tasks suitable for parallel dispatch (up to 3 concurrent) and propose them as a recommendation if the plan doesn't already group them. Distinguish required behavior or contract dependencies from shared-file scheduling constraints. Shared files require coordinated ownership, not automatically a dependency edge. Allow safe, authorized preparation while acceptance prerequisites are pending, without bypassing dependencies. Resolve dependency changes during planning; frozen dependencies remain binding during execution.

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 10 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 600000ms are capped to 600000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 10 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 600000ms are capped to 600000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
